title: Split a program into files
description:
Everything lives in `main.cpp` at the moment. Move the two conversion functions out into their own module:

1. Create `convert.h` (use the **+** next to the file tabs) containing a header guard and the two **declarations**.
2. Create `convert.cpp` containing `#include "convert.h"` and the two **definitions**.
3. In `main.cpp`, delete the function bodies and add `#include "convert.h"`.

The program reads a distance in kilometres and a weight in kilograms and must still print the same thing, for example for `10 70`:

```
6.21371 miles
154.323 pounds
```
hints: The header holds only the first line of each function, ending in a semicolon. The `.cpp` file holds the full functions.
If you see "already defined" from the linker, the function bodies are still in `main.cpp` as well as in `convert.cpp`. A function may only be defined once.
